# Devasadda Sutta (Iti 82 (It 3.33 PTS It 75))

**ID:** Iti 82 (It 3.33 PTS It 75)  
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Devasadda Sutta  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul2.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul2.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Devasadda Sutta* ("The Cry of the Gods", Iti 82; PTS It 75) is located in the third section (Tikanipāta) of the *Itivuttaka*. The sutta outlines three occasions on which celestial beings (*devas*) utter cries of joy and acclaim regarding the spiritual conduct and achievements of human beings (*tayo devesu devasaddā niccharanti*) [Windisch 1889]. Ernst Windisch's 1889 edition of the Pali text includes the prose conclusion of the discourse describing the third cry, raised when a noble disciple realizes awakening through higher knowledge and overcomes worldly struggles (*eso ariyasāvako vijitasaṅgāmo*), which is then followed by a summary verse (*disvā vijitasaṅgāmaṃ*) [Windisch 1889].
